name: NXP FRDM-MCXA153 development board
sources: MCXA153 data sheet MCXAP64M96FS3 Rev. 5.1, 16 October 2024 (features, no FPU, no AES or TRNG); FRDM-MCXA153 board user manual UM12012 Rev. 2.0, 12 February 2025 (kit contents, jumpers JP2, JP8, JP10, JP19, JP20, Figure 11 Arduino pinout, Table 8 current measurement); MCUXpresso SDK 26.09.00 driver list for frdmmcxa153 (crc, cdog, glikey; no crypto driver). All read 2026-10-07. Not measured on a board yet

columns.head: The chip: MCXA153VLH
items: Runs the program, up to 96 million steps a second (96 MHz). No floating-point unit, no DSP instructions
Holds the program, with error correction. Kept when the power is off
Working memory; 8 kB of it can have error correction. Same flash and RAM as the TI MSPM0G3507

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: Plain on/off pins on this 64-pin package. Most reach the Arduino, mikroBUS and Pmod headers
Serial text. LPUART0 goes to the USB debug chip, LPUART2 to the Arduino header D0 and D1
Sensor bus / fast bus for displays. Plus one I3C bus with a temperature sensor on it
16-bit, 3.2 million samples a second (4 million at 12-bit). No DAC to make a voltage
One FlexPWM with three pairs for a 3-phase motor, plus a quadrature encoder input
32-bit timers for timing and PWM, plus low-power and wake timers

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: MCU-Link on its own USB-C port (J15): flashing, debugging and a USB serial port
Second USB-C (J8) for the chip's own USB, RGB LED, reset, ISP and wake buttons, I3C temperature sensor
Arduino Uno layout (J1 to J4, sockets), mikroBUS (J5, J6). Pmod J7 not fitted
No floating-point unit, no AES, no random-number generator, no TrustZone, no radio. Hardware CRC only
Every float sum is a library call, like the M0+ parts. JP2 must stay fitted or the chip has no power
